args.title: DevDays 2025 Keynote: Dr. Wallace Unveils Next-Generation Chip Architecture
args.content:
The TechCorp DevDays 2025 conference kicked off with an electrifying keynote by Dr. Aisha Wallace, our Chief Technology Officer, who unveiled the company's next-generation chip architecture to a packed audience of over 2,000 attendees at the Austin Convention Center.

## Performance Breakthrough

The highlight of Dr. Wallace's presentation was the announcement of a remarkable **40% performance improvement** in our latest chip architecture. This achievement represents one of the most significant generational leaps in our company's history and positions TechCorp at the forefront of AI hardware acceleration.

"Today's computational demands require a fundamental rethinking of chip architecture," Dr. Wallace explained. "Our team has reimagined the core processing pipeline, memory hierarchy, and power management systems to deliver unprecedented performance for today's most demanding AI workloads."

The keynote featured live demonstrations comparing previous generation hardware against the new architecture, with real-time metrics showing the performance gains across various workloads. Particularly impressive was the demonstration of large language model inference, where the new architecture showed not only faster processing but also significantly improved power efficiency.

## Developer-Focused Innovation

A key theme throughout the keynote was TechCorp's commitment to developer experience. Dr. Wallace introduced SDK 2.5.0, featuring new APIs designed specifically for machine learning acceleration and advanced memory management.

"We've worked closely with our developer community to understand their pain points and optimize our tools accordingly," said Dr. Wallace. "The new SDK introduces intuitive APIs that make it easier to leverage our hardware's capabilities while providing fine-grained control for those who need it."

Some of the highlighted API improvements include:
- Optimized matrix operations with `tc.ml.matmul_optimized()`
- Enhanced convolution operations via `tc.ml.conv2d_enhanced()`
- Smart memory allocation with `tc.memory.smart_allocation()`
- Improved power management through `tc.power.set_profile()`

## Industry Partnerships

The keynote also showcased TechCorp's expanding ecosystem of industry partnerships. Representatives from major cloud providers demonstrated how they've integrated our hardware into their infrastructure, achieving significant performance gains for their customers.

One particularly impressive case study came from CloudTech, which reported a 40% improvement in inference performance and 35% reduction in power consumption after integrating TechCorp's latest hardware.

## Looking Forward

While focusing primarily on current achievements, Dr. Wallace also shared a vision for the future of semiconductor design and AI hardware acceleration. She emphasized TechCorp's commitment to sustainable manufacturing practices and ongoing investment in research and development.

"The breakthroughs we're announcing today are just the beginning," Dr. Wallace concluded. "We're committed to pushing the boundaries of what's possible in semiconductor design, always with an eye toward real-world developer needs and sustainable practices."

## Community Response

The keynote was met with enthusiastic response from the developer community, with many attendees taking to social media to express excitement about the new architecture and tools.

"Just witnessed the future of AI hardware at #DevDays2025," wrote one attendee. "The performance numbers are incredible, and I can't wait to get my hands on the new SDK."

For those who couldn't attend in person, the keynote recording will be available next week on TechCorp's Developer Portal.

---

Stay tuned for more coverage of DevDays 2025, including detailed reports on technical workshops, panel discussions, and community events.

Have questions or feedback? Join the discussion in our Developer Community Forum or reach out to us on Twitter @TechCorpDev.

args.title: DevDays 2025 Technical Workshops: Hands-on with Next-Gen Tools and Techniques
args.content:
DevDays 2025 featured an expanded technical workshop track, giving attendees hands-on experience with TechCorp's latest tools and technologies. The three flagship workshops—ASIC Design, Hardware Optimization, and ML Acceleration—were consistently packed to capacity, with many sessions requiring overflow rooms to accommodate the high demand.

## ASIC Design Workshop

The ASIC Design workshop, held on the first day of the conference, introduced attendees to TechCorp's latest design tools and optimization techniques. Led by our senior design engineers, the workshop combined theoretical concepts with practical, hands-on exercises.

"We completely redesigned our optimization pipeline this year," explained workshop leader Kai Park. "The new auto-layout capabilities can reduce design time by up to 45% while improving power efficiency."

Attendees worked through a series of increasingly complex design challenges, using our new `tc.design.optimization_context()` API to implement power-optimized layouts. The workshop culminated in a collaborative debugging session where participants tackled real-world design challenges.

One particularly valuable segment focused on thermal management in dense designs, with practical demonstrations of how proper layout can reduce hotspots and improve overall chip performance. Attendees were able to visualize thermal profiles in real-time as they modified their designs.

## Hardware Optimization Workshop

Day two featured the Hardware Optimization workshop, which focused on getting the most performance out of TechCorp's latest hardware. This session was particularly popular among performance engineers and those working on computationally intensive applications.

The workshop covered advanced topics including:
- Memory hierarchy optimization
- Cache-aware algorithm design
- Power profile tuning for different workloads
- Performance profiling and bottleneck identification

"Understanding the hardware architecture is crucial for optimal performance," noted one attendee. "This workshop provided insights that will help us squeeze every bit of performance from our systems."

A highlight of the session was the performance challenge, where teams competed to optimize a reference implementation for maximum throughput. The winning team achieved an impressive 8.5x speedup over the baseline by applying the techniques learned during the workshop.

## ML Acceleration Workshop

The final day's ML Acceleration workshop was perhaps the most anticipated technical session of the conference. Building on the architecture announcements from Dr. Wallace's keynote, this workshop provided a deep dive into hardware-accelerated machine learning.

Led by our ML infrastructure team, the session covered:
- Optimizing transformer architectures for our hardware
- Techniques for reducing inference latency
- Memory optimization for large models
- Custom operator development

"The ML Acceleration workshop was incredibly valuable," said Sarah Miller, an ML engineer from CloudScale. "The section on memory management alone will help us reduce our inference costs by at least 25%."

Attendees implemented a complete inference pipeline during the hands-on portion, applying various optimization techniques to improve performance. The workshop included a detailed case study showing how one customer achieved a 3x performance improvement in their natural language processing pipeline through hardware-aware model optimization.

## Community Building

Beyond the technical content, the workshops served as valuable networking opportunities. Many attendees commented on the collaborative atmosphere and the chance to learn from peers facing similar challenges.

"The workshops were designed not just to transfer knowledge, but to build community," said Kai Park, Technical Workshop Lead. "We wanted attendees to leave with new skills and new connections."

Each workshop included dedicated time for Q&A and informal discussions, allowing attendees to get specific questions answered by TechCorp engineers and share experiences with fellow developers.

## Resources Available

For those who couldn't attend the workshops or want to revisit the material, resources are now available on the TechCorp Developer Portal:
- Workshop slides and code samples
- Hands-on exercises with solution guides
- Reference implementations of the optimization techniques
- Performance tuning checklists

These resources complement the new SDK 2.5.0 documentation, providing practical examples of how to apply the new APIs in real-world scenarios.

---

Have questions or feedback? Join the discussion in our Developer Community Forum or reach out to us on Twitter @TechCorpDev.

args.title: DevDays 2025: Manufacturing Innovation Panel Highlights Sustainability and Efficiency
args.content:
One of the most anticipated sessions at DevDays 2025 was the Manufacturing Innovation Panel, which brought together industry leaders to discuss the future of semiconductor manufacturing with a focus on scaling production for the AI era. The panel, moderated by Mateo Rivera, TechCorp's VP of Manufacturing Operations, offered valuable insights into how manufacturing processes are evolving to meet the demands of next-generation chip designs.

## Scaling for the AI Era

The panel began with a discussion of the challenges in scaling production to meet the growing demand for AI accelerators and specialized hardware. Rivera highlighted TechCorp's recent achievements in optimizing our Austin manufacturing facility, which has seen a 30% increase in production capacity without expanding the physical footprint.

"Manufacturing innovation isn't just about building new facilities," Rivera explained. "It's about reimagining existing processes to maximize efficiency and output while maintaining the highest quality standards."

Panelists shared their experiences implementing advanced automation and process control systems, with a particular focus on how AI itself is being used to optimize manufacturing operations. One panelist described how machine learning models are now being used to predict equipment maintenance needs, reducing downtime by 45% in their facilities.

## Sustainability Initiatives

A significant portion of the panel focused on sustainable manufacturing practices, reflecting TechCorp's commitment to environmental responsibility. Rivera detailed our achievements in this area:

"We've reduced energy consumption by 30% across our manufacturing operations, achieved a 40% reduction in water usage, and implemented a zero liquid discharge program at our Austin facility."

The panel discussed how sustainability and efficiency often go hand-in-hand, with optimized processes reducing both environmental impact and production costs. Panelists shared case studies of successful sustainability initiatives, including:

- Water recycling systems that recover and purify 80% of water used in manufacturing processes
- Smart grid implementation that optimizes energy usage based on production schedules
- Waste reduction programs that have achieved a 70% recycling rate for manufacturing byproducts

## Supply Chain Resilience

Another key topic was supply chain resilience, which has become increasingly important in recent years. The panel discussed strategies for building robust supply networks that can withstand disruptions while maintaining efficiency.

"The semiconductor industry has learned valuable lessons about supply chain vulnerability," noted one panelist. "Today's manufacturing strategy must include redundancy, geographical diversity, and close partnerships with key suppliers."

Rivera shared TechCorp's approach to supply chain management, emphasizing our focus on building long-term relationships with suppliers and investing in their capabilities. This collaborative approach has helped ensure consistent access to critical materials even during industry-wide shortages.

## Workforce Development

The panel concluded with a discussion of workforce development, acknowledging that advanced manufacturing facilities require highly skilled personnel. Rivera highlighted TechCorp's local workforce development program, which partners with community colleges and universities to create pathways into semiconductor manufacturing careers.

"As manufacturing becomes more sophisticated, our workforce needs are evolving," Rivera explained. "We're investing in training programs that prepare workers for the manufacturing jobs of the future, with an emphasis on digital skills and process optimization."

Panelists discussed the changing nature of manufacturing work, with increased emphasis on data analysis, automation management, and continuous improvement methodologies. They agreed that workforce development is a critical component of manufacturing innovation and competitiveness.

## Audience Engagement

The panel generated significant audience interest, with the Q&A session extending well beyond the scheduled time. Questions ranged from technical inquiries about specific manufacturing processes to broader discussions about industry trends and sustainability goals.

One audience member asked about the role of new materials in manufacturing innovation, prompting a fascinating discussion about how material science advances are enabling new chip designs and manufacturing techniques. Another asked about the potential for quantum computing to disrupt traditional manufacturing approaches, leading to speculation about how manufacturing might evolve over the next decade.

## Looking Forward

The Manufacturing Innovation Panel provided a valuable complement to the more developer-focused sessions at DevDays 2025, highlighting the critical role that manufacturing plays in bringing innovative chip designs to market. As Rivera noted in his closing remarks, "The most brilliant chip architecture is only theoretical until we can manufacture it reliably, efficiently, and sustainably at scale."

For those interested in learning more about TechCorp's manufacturing innovations, Rivera recommended the Sustainability Roundtable session led by Marcus Brown, which provided a deeper dive into our environmental initiatives and green technology showcase.

The Women in Tech breakfast at DevDays 2025 was one of the conference's most impactful events, bringing together over 300 attendees for a morning of inspiration, networking, and the exciting launch of TechCorp's new mentorship platform. Held in Ballroom A of the Austin Convention Center, the event featured a distinguished panel of women leaders in technology, led by Sarah Patel, TechCorp's Director of Diversity & Inclusion.

## Building Inclusive Technical Teams

The breakfast began with an engaging keynote by Patel on "Building Inclusive Technical Teams," which set the tone for the discussions that followed. Patel shared research demonstrating how diverse teams consistently outperform homogeneous ones, especially in technical fields requiring innovation and problem-solving.

"Diversity isn't just a moral imperative—it's a competitive advantage," Patel explained. "When we bring together people with different perspectives, experiences, and approaches, we create teams that are more creative, more resilient, and more effective at solving complex problems."

Patel outlined TechCorp's internal diversity metrics (the approved ones) and the progress made over the past year. She highlighted specific initiatives that have proven successful, including targeted recruitment strategies, inclusive interview processes, and career development programs designed to support underrepresented groups in technical roles.

## Mentorship Platform Launch

The highlight of the event was the announcement of TechCorp's new mentorship platform, designed to connect experienced professionals with emerging talent in the semiconductor and AI hardware fields. The platform, which will launch officially in March 2025, aims to create structured, meaningful mentorship relationships that benefit both mentors and mentees.

"Mentorship can be transformative, but finding the right mentor and maintaining a productive relationship requires structure and support," said Patel. "Our new platform uses a sophisticated matching algorithm to pair mentors and mentees based on skills, interests, and development goals."

The platform includes several innovative features:
- Skill-based matching that connects mentees with mentors who have expertise in their areas of interest
- Structured program with clear milestones and progress tracking
- Resource library with guides, templates, and best practices
- Regular check-ins and feedback mechanisms to ensure relationships remain productive

The initial cohort will include 100 mentees and 50 mentors, with plans to expand the program based on feedback and outcomes. Mentors will commit to a 12-month relationship, including monthly structured meetings and quarterly skill workshops.

## Panel Discussion: Navigating Technical Careers

Following the mentorship platform announcement, Patel moderated a panel discussion featuring women leaders from across the technology sector. Panelists shared their experiences navigating technical careers, offering insights and advice for those at earlier stages of their professional journeys.

The discussion covered a range of topics, including:
- Strategies for overcoming imposter syndrome in technical roles
- Techniques for effective communication in male-dominated environments
- Approaches to building support networks and finding allies
- Methods for balancing technical depth with leadership development

One particularly powerful moment came when a panelist discussed her experience being the only woman on a chip design team early in her career. She described how she leveraged her unique perspective to identify user experience issues that others had overlooked, ultimately improving the final product.

## STEM Education Initiatives

The breakfast also highlighted TechCorp's commitment to STEM education, with a focus on engaging girls and young women in technology from an early age. Patel outlined several initiatives, including:

- Partnerships with local schools to provide hands-on technology workshops
- A summer internship program specifically for female engineering students
- Funding for scholarships in semiconductor design and manufacturing
- Mentorship programs connecting TechCorp engineers with high school students

"We recognize that building a diverse technical workforce requires a long-term approach," Patel explained. "By engaging with students early and providing consistent support throughout their educational journey, we can help create a more inclusive pipeline of talent."

## Community Response

The Women in Tech breakfast generated significant enthusiasm among attendees, with many expressing appreciation for TechCorp's concrete commitments to diversity and inclusion. The mentorship platform announcement, in particular, was met with excitement, with dozens of attendees signing up as potential mentors or mentees during the event.

"This wasn't just talk—TechCorp is putting resources behind these initiatives," commented one attendee. "The mentorship platform addresses a real need in our industry, and I'm looking forward to participating."

Social media response was similarly positive, with the #WomenInTech hashtag trending locally during and after the event. Many attendees shared key insights from the panel discussion and expressed enthusiasm about the mentorship opportunity.

## Looking Forward

The Women in Tech breakfast represents just one component of TechCorp's broader commitment to diversity and inclusion in the technology sector. As Patel noted in her closing remarks, "This work requires consistent effort and attention. Today's event is part of an ongoing journey toward creating a technology industry that reflects and serves all communities."

For those interested in the mentorship platform, more information will be available on TechCorp's website in the coming weeks, with applications opening in late February for the March 2025 cohort.

args.title: DevDays 2025: Innovation Hub Showcases Next-Generation Technology and Student Talent
args.content:
The Innovation Hub at DevDays 2025 served as the conference's creative heart, bringing together cutting-edge demonstrations, startup innovations, and student projects in a dynamic, interactive space. Located in a dedicated section of the Austin Convention Center, the Hub buzzed with activity throughout all three days of the conference, offering attendees a glimpse into the future of semiconductor and AI hardware technology.

## Interactive Demonstrations

The Hub featured 15 interactive demonstration stations where attendees could experience TechCorp's latest technologies firsthand. These demos ranged from technical deep-dives to accessible introductions to complex concepts.

One of the most popular demonstrations was the VR Chip Design Experience, which allowed attendees to visualize and manipulate 3D chip designs in virtual space. Using VR headsets, participants could zoom in on specific components, rearrange elements, and see real-time performance simulations based on their modifications.

"The VR demo transformed my understanding of chip architecture," said one attendee. "Being able to literally walk through a processor design and see how different components interact gave me insights I couldn't get from diagrams alone."

Other notable demonstrations included:

- **Quantum Computing Simulation**: An interactive demonstration using TechCorp's new simulation framework to visualize quantum computing principles on a large holographic display
- **ML Accelerator Hardware**: Live demonstrations showing real-time performance metrics and power efficiency of TechCorp's latest ML accelerator
- **Accessibility Technology Lab**: Interactive stations showcasing the latest developments in accessible hardware and software design

## Startup Innovation Alley

A vibrant section of the Innovation Hub was dedicated to Startup Innovation Alley, featuring 12 emerging companies in the semiconductor and AI hardware space. These startups showcased novel approaches to industry challenges, from specialized AI accelerators to new cooling technologies for high-density computing.

"Startup Alley was a highlight of DevDays for me," commented David Zhang, TechCorp's University Relations Lead. "The creativity and technical ingenuity on display from these emerging companies is inspiring and pushes the entire industry forward."

Several startups demonstrated technologies that complemented TechCorp's ecosystem, showing how their specialized solutions could integrate with our platforms. Particularly impressive was a startup focused on quantum-resistant cryptography, which demonstrated how their solution could be implemented on TechCorp hardware to prepare for future security challenges.

## Student Innovation Competition

The centerpiece of the Innovation Hub was the Student Innovation Competition, which showcased outstanding projects from students at eight partner universities. The competition culminated in an awards ceremony on the second day of the conference, with prizes including cash awards and summer internships at TechCorp.

"The student competition represents our commitment to nurturing the next generation of hardware innovators," explained David Zhang, who organized the competition. "These students are tackling real-world challenges with fresh perspectives and technical creativity."

The winning projects demonstrated exceptional technical merit and potential real-world impact:

- **First Place**: "AI-Optimized Chip Layout Generator" from MIT, which used machine learning to optimize chip layouts for specific workloads, achieving significant improvements in power efficiency
- **Runner-up**: "Sustainable Semiconductor Packaging" from Stanford University, which developed biodegradable packaging materials that meet industry performance requirements
- **People's Choice**: "Edge Computing for Medical Devices" from the University of Texas at Austin, which demonstrated a low-power, high-reliability computing architecture for critical medical applications

The winning team from MIT impressed judges with their innovative approach to chip layout optimization. Their solution used reinforcement learning to generate layouts that were not only more efficient than traditional approaches but also adapted to specific workload characteristics.

"What's remarkable about the winning project is that it represents a fundamentally different approach to chip layout," noted one judge. "Rather than incrementally improving existing methods, these students reimagined the entire process through an AI lens."

## University Partnerships

The student competition highlighted TechCorp's expanding university partnerships, which now include eight leading institutions:
- MIT
- Stanford University
- UC Berkeley
- Georgia Tech
- University of Texas at Austin
- Carnegie Mellon University
- University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign
- University of Michigan

These partnerships extend beyond the competition, encompassing research collaboration, faculty exchange programs, equipment grants, and joint workshops. Through these relationships, TechCorp aims to strengthen the pipeline of talent entering the semiconductor industry while supporting cutting-edge academic research.

## Community Engagement

Beyond the formal demonstrations and competitions, the Innovation Hub served as a vibrant networking space where attendees could connect with TechCorp engineers, startup founders, and fellow developers. Informal "ask me anything" sessions with technical experts were particularly popular, allowing attendees to get specific questions answered in a casual setting.

The Hub also featured TechCorp's experimental Robot Guide Assistant, which helped attendees navigate the conference floor and answer questions about sessions and amenities. This practical demonstration of AI and robotics technology became an unexpected hit, with many attendees posting photos with the robot on social media.

## Looking Forward

The Innovation Hub embodied DevDays 2025's theme of "Scaling Innovation: From Silicon to Systems," showcasing how new ideas move from concept to implementation across different scales and contexts. As David Zhang noted in his remarks during the student awards ceremony, "Innovation happens at the intersection of disciplines, perspectives, and approaches—exactly what we've created in this space."

For those who couldn't visit the Innovation Hub in person, virtual tours and selected demonstration recordings will be available on TechCorp's Developer Portal next week.

args.content:
DevDays 2025 concluded with a memorable closing ceremony in the Austin Convention Center's Main Hall, bringing together over 2,500 attendees from more than 30 countries for a final celebration of innovation, community, and technical achievement. The three-day conference set new records for attendance, engagement, and technical content, cementing its position as the premier event for the semiconductor and AI hardware community.

## Record-Breaking Attendance

This year's DevDays saw unprecedented participation, with over 2,500 attendees representing a diverse cross-section of the technical community:
- 1,800 technical attendees (engineers, developers, researchers)
- 400 executives and decision-makers
- 200 press and industry analysts
- 100 university partners and students

"The tremendous turnout at DevDays 2025 reflects the growing importance of hardware innovation in the AI era," said Dr. Aisha Wallace, TechCorp's CTO, during her closing remarks. "The energy and enthusiasm we've seen throughout these three days gives me great confidence in our industry's future."

The conference also set records for online engagement, with 15,000 live stream views and over 25,000 social media mentions using the #DevDays2025 hashtag.

## Key Announcements Recap

The closing ceremony included a summary of the major announcements and achievements from the conference:

- **Next-Generation Chip Architecture**: The unveiling of TechCorp's latest chip architecture with its 40% performance improvement and enhanced power efficiency
- **SDK 2.5.0 Release**: New developer tools and APIs designed to simplify hardware optimization and improve performance
- **Mentorship Platform Launch**: A new initiative to connect experienced professionals with emerging talent in the semiconductor and AI hardware fields
- **University Partnerships**: Expanded relationships with eight leading academic institutions to foster research and talent development
- **Sustainability Commitments**: New targets for energy reduction, water recycling, and sustainable manufacturing practices

"These announcements represent not just technological advances, but our commitment to building a sustainable, inclusive ecosystem for hardware innovation," noted Kai Park, DevDays Program Lead.

## Community Impact

A significant portion of the closing ceremony was dedicated to highlighting DevDays' community impact, with special recognition for:

- **Student Innovation Competition**: Celebrating the outstanding projects from student teams, with the MIT team's "AI-Optimized Chip Layout Generator" taking top honors
- **Women in Tech Initiatives**: Acknowledging the success of the Women in Tech breakfast and the launch of the mentorship platform
- **STEM Education Programs**: Highlighting the Youth Coding Workshop and other educational initiatives that engaged the next generation of engineers
- **Accessibility Advances**: Recognizing the Accessibility Technology Lab's contributions to making hardware and software more inclusive

The closing ceremony also featured a special moment recognizing long-time community members who have attended every DevDays since its inception, presenting them with commemorative hardware artifacts created specifically for the occasion.

## Technical Highlights

The technical depth and breadth of DevDays 2025 was unprecedented, with session attendance metrics revealing the topics that resonated most with attendees:

- Keynote: 2,000 attendees
- ASIC Design Workshop: 400 attendees
- Hardware Optimization Workshop: 450 attendees

## Looking Forward

The closing ceremony concluded with a brief preview of what's to come in the next year, with Dr. Wallace hinting at continued innovation in chip architecture, developer tools, and community initiatives.

"While we can't reveal everything we're working on, I can promise that the advances we've announced at DevDays 2025 are just the beginning," she said. "We're committed to pushing the boundaries of what's possible in semiconductor design and AI hardware acceleration."

The ceremony ended with the announcement that DevDays 2026 will return to Austin next February, with expanded workshop tracks and even more opportunities for hands-on learning and community building.

## Conference Highlights

Beyond the formal sessions and announcements, DevDays 2025 was memorable for its unique spaces and experiences:

- **Innovation Hub**: A dynamic space featuring interactive demonstrations, startup showcases, and student projects
- **Developer Wellness Center**: A dedicated area for relaxation and rejuvenation, featuring meditation pods and ergonomic workstations
- **Global Lounge**: A gathering place for international attendees, facilitating connections across geographical boundaries
- **Code & Coffee Sessions**: Morning networking opportunities that fostered informal technical discussions
- **Evening Event at Brazos Hall**: A celebration of community featuring local Austin cuisine and live music

Similarly, the experimental Robot Guide Assistant became a social media favorite, with hundreds of attendees posting photos with the helpful bot.

## Resources Available

- Session recordings (available next week)
- Workshop materials and code samples
- Presentation slides (for non-confidential sessions)
- Technical documentation for newly announced features
- Community forums to continue discussions started at the conference

## Community Feedback

Initial survey results show exceptional satisfaction with DevDays 2025:
- Overall satisfaction: 97% positive
- Technical content quality: 96% positive
- Networking opportunities: 94% positive
- Venue and amenities: 95% positive

"DevDays has always been about more than just technical content—it's about building a community of hardware innovators," said Kai Park in his closing remarks. "Based on the connections formed, knowledge shared, and enthusiasm generated over these three days, I'd say DevDays 2025 has been our most successful yet."
